subject: Global exec demo slot consolidation & DST risk for Oct 30

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Global exec demo — target Oct 30 (slot proposals + DST note)

Hi Suzanne —

Great to connect last week. Per our conversation the exec demo target window is the week of Oct 25–31, and Orbital’s execs prefer the single consolidated session on Oct 30 if we can make it work across regions.

I pulled together a compact slot matrix (attached) with times converted to UTC, PDT/EDT, CET, and JST. Important callout: Oct 30 sits right in the autumn DST transition period for EMEA/US (EU clocks roll back the last weekend in October) — that can shift local labels by an hour between calendars. To avoid confusion I recommend we:  
- Propose slots in UTC in the calendar invite and include local conversions in the invite body.
- Add an explicit note in the invite: “Times shown in UTC — local time may shift due to daylight savings rules.”
- Offer an APAC-recorded follow-up for any execs who can’t make the consolidated session.

Attached: proposed_slot_matrix_oct30.csv (UTC-first) and a sample exec_availability.ics for the preferred slot.

Can you confirm general availability constraints for Orbital’s US/EU/APAC execs (Tom, Suzanne, and others)? If Oct 30 is hard we can target Oct 29 as a fallback.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa for calendar ops and Aditya for a short tech sync pre-demo.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

Subject: Re: Global exec demo — target Oct 30 (slot proposals + DST note)

Vivek —

Thanks for the matrix and the DST heads-up — good catch. A couple of constraints from our side:
- Tom (APAC exec) prefers local morning (JST 09:00–11:00) on either Oct 30 or Oct 31.
- Our EU execs are tricky around Oct 30 this year because some are traveling; they asked for blocks between 08:30–11:00 CET. Note that CET will revert from CEST on the last Sunday of October, so a calendar invite labeled “10:00 CET” could be ambiguous for attendees depending on how their calendar interprets the date.

Two asks:
1) Would Redwood be able to run the main consolidated demo at a single UTC time and record it for APAC, plus schedule a live APAC-friendly follow-up the next local morning if needed?
2) Can you add an explicit timezone note in the invite and send invites as UTC to reduce automatic calendar re-labeling?

If you can propose 3 UTC slots that map to the EU 09:00–11:00 window and APAC evening, we’ll confirm with Tom and the board.

— Suzanne
Suzanne Lee
Head of Product, Orbital AI

Hi Suzanne — Vivek —

Thanks — uploading the UTC-first slot matrix to Drive and attaching an .ics for the primary option per Vivek’s recommendation. Quick summary of three slots I’m proposing (all shown in UTC first; local conversions in parentheses):
- Option A: 2027-10-30 13:00 UTC (EDT 09:00 / CET 15:00 / JST 22:00) — good for EU morning, early US, late APAC (record + offer APAC follow-up)
- Option B: 2027-10-30 15:00 UTC (EDT 11:00 / CET 17:00 / JST 00:00 next day) — better US/EU overlap, APAC late-night
- Option C (fallback): 2027-10-29 16:00 UTC (EDT 12:00 / CET 18:00 / JST 01:00 next day) — earlier fallback if Oct 30 is impossible

Notes:  
- I’ve emphasized UTC in the invite body and attached the exec_availability.ics that uses a UTC stamp so calendar clients are less likely to auto-shift labels.
- If APAC execs can’t join live we’ll push a recorded session and block a 30-min live Q&A the next APAC morning (we’ll propose Oct 31 08:30 JST).

I’ll prepare calendar invites as UTC and mark them: "Time shown in UTC — please verify local time after daylight savings changes."
